summary: The run entered Act 2 with a workable offensive and defensive core, but accumulated severe HP losses throughout Act 1 and reached the final fight at 18/80 HP. Runic Pyramid then made hand quality and exhaust management especially important, while the final combat opened with a full turn of defense and no damage against three enemies. The immediate loss was in combat, but the underlying pattern was insufficient HP margin and a deck that became harder to cycle under Pyramid.

lessons.title: Do not spend the opening turn entirely on defense when the enemy board is still healthy
lessons.situation: When starting a fight at low HP against several enemies, especially when attacks are incoming, compare full-block lines against immediately weakening or killing one target.
lessons.lesson: Avoid automatically chaining every defensive card on turn one. In the final fight, Power Through, Shrug It Off, and Defend consumed all three energy without damaging an enemy; prefer a legal damage or debuff line when it can reduce the number or severity of future attacks, unless the state clearly requires full defense.
evidence_points: Turn 1 began at 18/80 HP with three enemies present, including two with ATTACK intent and Taskmaster with ATTACK_DEBUFF intent.
The chosen sequence was Power Through, Shrug It Off, and Defend, leaving all enemies at full HP; after ending the turn, player HP was 14/80.
On turn 2, all three enemies showed ATTACK_DEBUFF intent, while the first damaging play was not made until Pommel Strike.
lessons.reasoning: The log establishes that the all-defense line did not remove or weaken any enemy before the next enemy actions and cost 4 HP immediately. The exact best counterfactual is not fully recoverable, but the reusable correction is to avoid zero-damage openings when a low-HP fight has multiple active enemies and legal offensive alternatives.

lessons.title: Keep the Pyramid deck tighter and prioritize exhaust or hand control
lessons.situation: After obtaining Runic Pyramid, evaluate every additional card by whether it improves a retained hand or helps remove dead cards and generated wounds.
lessons.lesson: With Runic Pyramid, favor skip/removal and reliable exhaust or hand-management tools over broadly adding more cards. A large retained hand can preserve Wounds and dilute the important cards needed to stabilize a turn.
evidence_points: Runic Pyramid was chosen as the Act 1 boss relic.
The final deck contained 28 cards, including four Strikes and four Defends, while only one Strike was removed at the Act 1 shop.
In the final combat, the hand contained multiple Wounds; True Grit+ was used to select a Wound for exhaust, showing that retained clutter was an active problem.
lessons.reasoning: Pyramid makes dead cards persist rather than naturally leaving the hand at turn end. The final build and combat state both show that the deck still contained substantial basic-card density and generated Wounds, so future additions should be more selective and should improve exhaust, draw, or hand quality.

lessons.title: Protect an HP buffer before continuing Act 1 fights or taking marginal upgrades
lessons.situation: When repeated combats have reduced HP into the teens or low twenties, treat survival margin as the primary resource before choosing further combat paths or a smith.
lessons.lesson: Do not rely on late healing to recover from a long sequence of low-HP combats. After reaching very low HP, prioritize a recovery opportunity when available and only smith when the remaining HP buffer can safely support the next fights and boss.
evidence_points: The run began the first combat at 56/80 HP after taking the Neow damage option, then reached 21/80 by Act 1 Floor 8 and 13/80 by Floor 11.
The run did rest at 13/80 on Floor 12, but later chose smith at 23/80 on Floor 15 before the Act 1 boss.
The Hexaghost fight began at 23/80 and ended with the player at 22/80, while Act 2 later reached the final combat at 18/80.
lessons.reasoning: Although the run survived the boss, the repeated low-HP states left little margin for ordinary combat variance and made the final Act 2 fights much less forgiving. The lesson is to convert early damage and subsequent attrition into a deliberate recovery plan rather than treating each campfire upgrade as safe at low HP.
